scope.method: A coordinator reviewed the commit and test matrix. Three independent source reviews covered Linux confinement, memory lifetime and Unix/Windows/Apple IPC. The coordinator checked candidates against local code and operating-system contracts and kept runtime confirmations distinct from static findings.

findings.title: Linux secret-memory allocation and concurrent fork share an inheritance window
findings.reproduction: Static control-flow and contract review of the cited lines at the reviewed commit. The native public diagnostic identified the active backend only. No secret transfer was tested.
findings.expected: Child exclusion must hold for a buffer reported out of children.
findings.observed: During successful secretmem allocation, the shared backing file is temporarily open across fork. DONTFORK affects a mapping and CLOEXEC takes effect at exec. Neither revokes an already inherited descriptor.
findings.impact: A concurrent fork without immediate exec can retain the same backing object into which the parent later places secret bytes. The private anonymous fallback has different sharing semantics. The diagnostic confirmed use of secretmem on the host, without testing disclosure.
findings.recommendedFix: Use the private anonymous backend when fork can run concurrently. Reserve shared secretmem for a fork-free worker or a caller with an enforceable fork-free lifecycle. Make this precondition part of the guarantee.
findings.requiredVerification: Check both backends, allocation lifecycle and process model using public fixtures on supported Linux kernels. Verify the claimed scope before accepting sensitive input.

findings.title: Unix worker acknowledges isolation after incomplete descriptor cleanup
findings.reproduction: Static control-flow and contract review of the cited lines at the reviewed commit.
findings.expected: A worker advertising clean inherited channels must know that all unintended descriptors were closed.
findings.observed: After the bulk close fails or is unavailable, directory-open failure silently returns, directory-entry errors are discarded and close results are ignored. Startup still sends the protection bits.
findings.impact: If the worker inherited a writable file or socket and fallback enumeration fails, the strict handshake can accept secrets with the channel still present. The normal Linux close_range path is unaffected.
findings.recommendedFix: Propagate the cleanup outcome before sending the handshake. Use a supported close-from operation or a verified fallback, with explicit handling of the listing descriptor and OS close semantics.
findings.requiredVerification: Verify clean startup and startup refusal on incomplete cleanup with public descriptors, including the fallback on macOS.

findings.title: Linux tracer evidence for one thread is reported process-wide
findings.reproduction: Static control-flow and contract review of the cited lines at the reviewed commit.
findings.expected: A positive process-wide result requires evidence covering prior tracers on all relevant threads.
findings.observed: TracerPid is read only for the calling thread. Setting the process non-dumpable restricts new access and does not detach existing tracers. Linux ptrace attaches per thread.
findings.impact: A multithreaded caller can pass a required NoMemoryReading check despite an existing tracer of a different thread sharing its memory. The single-threaded worker avoids this particular mismatch.
findings.recommendedFix: Establish the property before concurrency, or implement a sound process-wide check under a controlled thread lifecycle. Otherwise mark it unverified for a multithreaded caller.
findings.requiredVerification: Cover single-thread initialization, multithread scope and unavailable thread inventory. A process-wide positive result must refer to the entire claimed scope.

findings.title: Windows worker pipe ends are briefly inheritable by unrelated launches
findings.reproduction: Static control-flow and contract review of the cited lines at the reviewed commit.
findings.expected: Only the designated worker and its parent may hold secret request and response pipe handles.
findings.observed: Both ends are created inheritable. Inheritance is cleared later on the parent ends. The explicit handle list limits inheritance for the worker launch only.
findings.impact: A separate child spawned concurrently by the same parent using broad handle inheritance can receive an IPC endpoint. This applies to applications with such process-launch behavior. No Windows runtime observation.
findings.recommendedFix: Keep inheritable ends in a dedicated launch broker with controlled child creation, or enforce coordinated allowlisted inheritance across all launchers in the process. Creating parent ends non-inheritable also narrows the window.
findings.requiredVerification: Validate handle ownership during concurrent independent benign launches on Windows. Verify only designated actors can own the IPC endpoints.

findings.title: macOS accepts local probe denials without a confirmed sandbox profile
findings.reproduction: Static control-flow and contract review of the cited lines at the reviewed commit.
findings.expected: A strict, process-wide file or network restriction requires confirmation of the intended profile or independently equivalent policy.
findings.observed: The result of sandbox_init is used only to free an error message. A permission denial creating one temporary file can come from its directory. A single UDP loopback check likewise cannot characterize an unknown profile.
findings.impact: When profile installation fails, an ordinary pre-existing directory restriction can satisfy NoFileChanges while other directories remain writable. A caller requiring the flag can then admit secret input.
findings.recommendedFix: Track actual successful profile installation, including re-entry, and combine it with the intended readbacks. Return unknown on an unverified external sandbox.
findings.requiredVerification: On macOS verify first success, repeat entry, and refused installation with independently restricted probe locations in disposable processes.

findings.title: Signal-domain isolation can satisfy a stricter self-only claim
findings.reproduction: Static control-flow and contract review of the cited lines at the reviewed commit.
findings.expected: Evidence must distinguish self-only addressing, a Landlock domain boundary and unsupported enforcement.
findings.observed: A successful seccomp installation plus Landlock ABI support can stand in for a failed Landlock application. An enforced Landlock signal scope groups processes. The self-only filter separately embeds the installing process ID, which is inherited across fork.
findings.impact: A required ForeignSignalsRefused result can mean separate things and can be positive without the advertised restriction. A child cannot interpret an inherited fixed-ID filter as its own self-only policy.
findings.recommendedFix: Distinguish confirmed signal-domain scope from self-only mode, track enforcement separately from availability, and bind or restrict the supported process lifecycle.
findings.requiredVerification: Test each enforcement state independently, including unavailable Landlock, repeated entry and supported descendant semantics. Verify the strict requirement accepts only the requested property.

findings.title: Unsupported speculation control is accepted as confirmed mitigation
findings.reproduction: Static control-flow and contract review of the cited lines at the reviewed commit.
findings.expected: A positive mitigation claim needs a confirmed protection or a supported indication that the CPU is unaffected.
findings.observed: For indirect branches the implementation accepts ENODEV. The kernel defines it as an unsupported selector, while a successful zero return identifies an unaffected CPU. The code also groups ordinary disable with irreversible disable.
findings.impact: The strict requirement or detailed report can overstate speculative-execution mitigation on particular architectures and configurations. No leakage was observed.
findings.recommendedFix: Represent unsupported as unknown and distinguish reversible from permanent disable where the public contract promises permanence. Permit platform-specific equivalents only with evidence.
findings.requiredVerification: Validate the mapping from independent kernel results to supported, unaffected, reversible, irreversible and unknown statuses.

findings.title: Protected stack properties cannot be required before secret work
findings.reproduction: Static control-flow and contract review of the cited lines at the reviewed commit.
findings.expected: A caller relying on exclusion or locking must verify those properties before invoking its callback.
findings.observed: Page advice and locking are best effort. Apple explicitly reports no per-mapping dump exclusion. The callback runs before the caller receives even the lock result. Dump and child flags are omitted from StackRun.
findings.impact: A standalone caller on Apple, or a caller under Linux policy or quota restrictions, can put secret temporaries on a stack that falls short of the documented protection.
findings.recommendedFix: Provide a pre-callback required-properties policy and report the mapping outcomes. Identify when a separately confirmed process-wide measure supplies an equivalent guarantee.
findings.requiredVerification: On Linux and Apple assert that missing required flags prevent callback entry. Test the best-effort API and normal/panic completion separately.

findings.title: Stack wiping assumes every post-pthread byte is an initialized Rust u8
findings.reproduction: Static control-flow and contract review of the cited lines at the reviewed commit.
findings.expected: Final wiping must be valid for arbitrary used stack memory and may begin only once all thread access has ended.
findings.observed: The code forms a mutable slice of initialized bytes over an entire used stack. Arbitrary frames can contain uninitialized storage or padding even though the original mapping was zero-filled. pthread_join's return value is discarded.
findings.impact: The unsafe conversion lacks an initialization proof for a safe public API. Successful ordinary tests do not establish this invariant. No optimizer-induced leak was observed.
findings.recommendedFix: Use a write-only raw wipe or a MaybeUninit byte representation with an optimization-resistant wipe. Establish successful join before releasing the backing allocation and job.
findings.requiredVerification: Review lifetime and initialization invariants, check generated wipe code, and exercise normal and panic paths on supported Unix runtimes.

findings.title: ClosedSecret forgets the previous access mode after a refused reseal
findings.reproduction: Static control-flow and contract review of the cited lines at the reviewed commit.
findings.expected: A mutable reference or destructor wipe requires confirmed write access, including after OS protection failures.
findings.observed: A read-only opening followed by refused resealing leaves the closed boolean false. A subsequent refused read-write transition can therefore be ignored even if the mapping is still read-only.
findings.impact: When OS policy refuses both transitions, a write or cleanup can fault. The condition does not establish disclosure and was not observed on this host.
findings.recommendedFix: Track actual access permissions explicitly and distinguish unsupported backends. Refuse any operation whose required access cannot be established before producing the reference or wiping.
findings.requiredVerification: Exercise policy-refused transitions from read-only state, including drop and callback unwinding, with public data.

findings.title: Windows dynamic-code status ignores permitted exemptions
findings.reproduction: Static control-flow and contract review of the cited lines at the reviewed commit.
findings.expected: A process-wide permanent prohibition must account for Windows policy exceptions.
findings.observed: Readback tests ProhibitDynamicCode alone. A policy may also set AllowThreadOptOut or AllowRemoteDowngrade.
findings.impact: A strict requirement can accept a preconfigured and weaker dynamic-code policy. The scope is installations carrying those mitigation settings.
findings.recommendedFix: Classify opt-out and downgrade flags explicitly and require the promised properties before reporting strict success.
findings.requiredVerification: Validate the official policy combinations on supported Windows versions and expose partial coverage explicitly.

findings.title: Dropping a worker can wait forever after rejecting a large reply
findings.reproduction: Static control-flow and contract review of the cited lines at the reviewed commit.
findings.expected: A rejected, oversized answer should permit prompt disposal and reaping of the worker.
findings.observed: The parent rejects the advertised size, retains the unread output pipe, closes only the input and waits. The child can be blocked writing the rest of a legitimate answer.
findings.impact: When the remaining reply exceeds pipe capacity, both sides can wait indefinitely. The standard test uses a 100-byte reply that fits in the pipe.
findings.recommendedFix: Close both IPC directions before waiting. Define a bounded shutdown policy for broken workers and mark partial transport failures terminal.
findings.requiredVerification: Use a normal large public response with a bounded test deadline on Unix and Windows. Verify prompt return and child reaping.

findings.title: Fork-based work inside a protected stack may lose its active stack
findings.reproduction: Static control-flow and contract review of the cited lines at the reviewed commit.
findings.expected: The callback contract should identify supported ways to launch children safely.
findings.observed: The active stack is configured to be wiped or excluded on fork. A non-terminal Unix Worker start registers a pre_exec closure, where the child needs usable execution state before exec.
findings.impact: A caller that starts a fork-based operation from the protected stack can lose its active return frames in the child. Normal stack-only tests do not exercise this composition.
findings.recommendedFix: Document and enforce the relevant process lifecycle where feasible. Start workers outside this stack or use a launch design independent of its post-fork frames.
findings.requiredVerification: Check supported process-launch combinations with plain public operations on Linux and Apple and document any unsupported ones.

findings.title: MemoryLocked loses a successful process lock on re-entry
findings.reproduction: New public Linux diagnostic in AUD-001-harnesses/report_state.rs. See report-state.log and the static implementation.
findings.expected: Repeated default entry should report a still-effective process lock or explicitly describe uncertainty.
findings.observed: memory_locked reads the options of this call. The public Linux diagnostic observed true then false without an unlock, with VmLck still nonzero.
findings.impact: Health reporting or strict checks can reject a correctly locked worker. The existing test only validates VmLck if the flag happens to be true.
findings.recommendedFix: Track established state within the supported process lifecycle and invalidate it appropriately on fork or external changes. Distinguish requested, observed and unverified.
findings.requiredVerification: Check positive and negative configurations under known quotas, repeated entry, and the documented scope of external changes.

findings.title: open_channels can return an apparently complete partial inventory
findings.reproduction: Static control-flow and contract review of the cited lines at the reviewed commit.
findings.expected: Callers need to distinguish a complete inventory from an unavailable or inconclusive scan.
findings.observed: Entry and fstat failures can silently remove descriptors. F_GETFL failure becomes a non-writable classification. A writable nonregular handle can be labelled WritableFile. Concurrent changes also limit a live snapshot.
findings.impact: An isolation UI can omit a real channel, mislabel a non-file FD, or interpret an incomplete scan as a clean report. Windows and WASM explicitly return None.
findings.recommendedFix: Report incomplete scans and unknown kinds, handle transient disappearance separately, and identify regular files explicitly. Document snapshot scope.
findings.requiredVerification: Check incomplete enumeration, harmless special descriptors and concurrent lifecycle changes. Confirm the listing's own transient descriptor is excluded.

findings.title: Detailed protection reports describe possible proofs as if observed
findings.reproduction: New public Linux diagnostic in AUD-001-harnesses/report_state.rs. See report-state.log and the static implementation.
findings.expected: Each result should tell the integrator what was observed and the scope of the evidence.
findings.observed: Proof strings are static by protection type even for an unrequested or refused protection. On Windows several attempted measures, including reporting and integrity restrictions, have no corresponding per-measure outcome.
findings.impact: The diagnostic observed holds=false with proof='mlockall accepted'. A UI can display evidence that was never obtained on that call.
findings.recommendedFix: Separate mechanisms from observed outcomes. Represent applied, refused, unsupported, unrequested and unknown, including scope. Identify Windows measures with no readback.
findings.requiredVerification: Check every advertised measure against actual positive, refused and unsupported states, including serialization across the worker handshake.

findings.title: Oversized protected stack requests overflow during rounding
findings.reproduction: Static control-flow and contract review of the cited lines at the reviewed commit.
findings.expected: An unrepresentable requested stack size should return an error without running work.
findings.observed: next_multiple_of is unchecked near usize::MAX. Depending on overflow checks, it can panic or wrap and select the minimum stack.
findings.impact: A caller-supplied size can produce a different result from the documented minimum-size contract.
findings.recommendedFix: Use checked rounding and reject unrepresentable or platform-invalid sizes before thread creation.
findings.requiredVerification: Check boundary values in checked and optimized builds without allocating a huge buffer.

findings.title: Hard-coded MCL_ONFAULT is incorrect on some Linux architectures
findings.reproduction: Static control-flow and contract review of the cited lines at the reviewed commit.
findings.expected: The lock flag must match the target's Linux UAPI.
findings.observed: The crate uses 4 unconditionally. Linux headers on PowerPC and SPARC define 0x8000.
findings.impact: Whole-process locking may be refused despite kernel support on those targets, outside the six lint targets.
findings.recommendedFix: Use an authoritative target binding or correct cfg-specific constants and define the supported targets explicitly.
findings.requiredVerification: Check against UAPI headers and cross-build the affected targets if supported.

findings.title: Windows work areas skip a potentially available page lock
findings.reproduction: Static control-flow and contract review of the cited lines at the reviewed commit.
findings.expected: Strict work-area locking should use existing working-set allowance where Windows permits it.
findings.observed: A refused working-set enlargement short-circuits VirtualLock even if the current allowance could hold the pages. The ordinary Secret path already attempts VirtualLock independently.
findings.impact: Under a restricted process policy a strict work-area allocation can be rejected unnecessarily.
findings.recommendedFix: Attempt VirtualLock within available allowance independently of successful growth. Restore only quota actually increased.
findings.requiredVerification: On Windows verify both available and exhausted allowance when a working-set change is refused.

findings.title: Windows cleanup is attempted on a potentially uninitialized attribute list
findings.reproduction: Static control-flow and contract review of the cited lines at the reviewed commit.
findings.expected: Destroy a process attribute list only after its initialization succeeds.
findings.observed: Cleanup is unconditional after the second InitializeProcThreadAttributeList call, including the path where initialization itself fails. Zero-filled storage does not establish the API precondition.
findings.impact: An OS startup failure can lead to an invalid cleanup call rather than the intended clean error.
findings.recommendedFix: Guard destruction with successful initialization and preserve the underlying initialization or update error.
findings.requiredVerification: Check initialization failure and later attribute-update failure as separate cleanup paths.

findings.title: Keystroke serialization leaves wiping to a caller that is promised a wipe
findings.reproduction: Static control-flow and contract review of the cited lines at the reviewed commit.
findings.expected: The owner of all five scratch bytes and the time of wiping should be explicit.
findings.observed: The serializer accepts caller-owned storage, writes only a prefix and cannot wipe it after transmission. Reuse for a shorter event can leave old UTF-8 bytes in the tail.
findings.impact: A GUI following the text literally may retain typed bytes in ordinary memory. SecretLine separately wipes its own encoding scratch.
findings.recommendedFix: Return a zeroizing scoped owner or document and demonstrate wiping the whole caller buffer on every exit after sending.
findings.requiredVerification: Check reuse across different encoded lengths and error exits. Confirm that the transport receives only the used prefix.

findings.title: Usage guidance overstates disk guarantees and lists shipped restrictions as planned
findings.reproduction: Static control-flow and contract review of the cited lines at the reviewed commit.
findings.expected: Integration guidance must agree with platform guarantees and the shipped options.
findings.observed: The README literally promises that no secret ever reaches disk alongside exceptions. The technical notes describe file locks and sendmsg switches as future work, and omit self-only seccomp in that summary. The Windows overview also omits earlier non-debug read handles.
findings.impact: Applications may choose the wrong policy or promise protection from hibernation, crash capture, or old handles beyond the documented API.
findings.recommendedFix: Correct the contradictory sentences and state pre-existing process/thread handle, snapshot, crash and caller-copy limits next to the summaries.
findings.requiredVerification: Compare each user-facing protection against its implementation and tests on current and older kernels.

guidance: Use a fresh single-threaded, fork-free worker where the platform supports one. Verify required protections and intended channel ownership before admitting test or user secrets. Mobile integrations need their own platform-specific isolation and device evidence.

Protect long-lived secrets and Argon2 work areas explicitly. Determine whether a given allocation fits the lock quota. A strict configuration that requires locked work memory must refuse the sensitive operation when it cannot obtain it. Keep whole-process locking opt-in.

The current worker protocol accepts a u32 byte count and makes a non-fallible allocation on the receiving side. Define application-specific request/reply maxima, use fallible allocation for untrusted sizes, and retire broken transports on partial I/O.
Measure names should distinguish socket creation, usable network connections, and inherited channels. A token capability check is evidence about policy, not an observed network connection test.
Forked descendants should not reuse copied protected-buffer objects or cached lock flags. Memory locks are not inherited and mappings can be wiped or absent.

Verify the integration against native OS crash handling. Windows reports no whole-process NoCoreDumps and Windows Error Reporting can retain stacks and registers. WASM offers buffer wiping only. SIGKILL and abort do not execute Rust Drop. Hibernation and VM snapshots require OS policy.
limitations: Native runtime evidence is limited to Linux x86_64 on kernel 7.0.0-43-generic. Clippy type-checked other targets. No native Windows, macOS, iOS, Android or WASM runtime, installer, link test or end-to-end consuming application was exercised.

The ordinary suite, diagnostic and code review do not certify complete memory erasure, impossibility of disclosure, or resistance to privileged OS access. No secret transfer or exploit was demonstrated. No formal proof, sanitizer or disassembly campaign was performed.
The host used a fresh target directory and offline locked dependencies. Upstream dependency internals and current transitive advisories were not audited.

The library tests did not cover terminal password entry in a consuming application, integration with a steganography application, browser interfaces, suspend images, VM snapshots or device-wide crash collectors.
